disposition_reason: Strontium-90 activity concentrations in soil and vegetation from Fukushima-affected hot spots; per-sample values only in supplement, summary values in text.

study.origin: eastern Japanese coast including sites near Fukushima Daiichi
study.method: strontium-resin separation and liquid scintillation counting; HPGe gamma spectrometry for cesium
study.qa: IAEA-373 grass reference material; strontium-85 yield tracer (92.4 to 98.2 percent recovery)

material.label_as_printed: Soil and vegetation samples, Japanese hot spots

findings.notes: Activity concentration of strontium-90, decay corrected to 11 March 2011; not a mass concentration.

regulatory_or_exposure: Japanese authorities assumed strontium-90 activity of no more than 10 percent of cesium-137 activity for food regulatory limits; no sample in this study exceeded that ratio (Results, p. 4).
non_numeric_findings: Strontium-90 is described as accumulating in bone with potential to cause leukemia or skeletal cancer (Introduction, p. 1).
